title: Impact of Sole Footwear on Toddler Gait Parameters
author: Cylie Williams
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bq6dmza6
materials: Study design: A quasi-experimental pre-post design.

steps.title: Prepare Footwear
steps.instruction: Modify footwear to accommodate reflective markers by cutting small holes in specific locations.

substeps.instruction: Cut small holes in the posterior aspect of the heel, medially over the navicular region, laterally over the cuboid region, and dorsally in the midfoot region.
Ensure no fixtures (e.g., straps or elastic) are modified during the cutting process.

steps.title: Habituate Toddlers and Fit Footwear
steps.instruction: Allow toddlers to explore the testing environment and verify footwear fit.

substeps.instruction: Encourage toddlers to explore the laboratory to familiarize themselves with the setting.
Check footwear sizing to ensure appropriate fit under the ankle and the adjustable strap.
Verify that the footwear length is approximately 1cm from the longest toe.

steps.title: Place Markers
steps.instruction: Apply reflective markers to the skin and footwear using a standardized placement protocol.

substeps.instruction: Semi-permanently mark the toddler's legs and clothing to ensure consistent replacement of loose markers.
Adhere reflective markers to the skin over the semi-permanent marks using double-sided tape.
Use 14mm markers for all pre-determined body locations except the feet, and 9.5mm markers for the feet.

Place markers on both sides of the body at: posterior calcaneus, dorsal aspect of the midfoot, medial aspect of the navicular, lateral aspect of the cuboid, medial and lateral malleoli, medial and lateral knee joint, anterior and posterior superior iliac spines, mid-lateral thigh, mid-lateral lower leg shank, anterior aspect of each shoulder, and C7 at the back of the neck.
Ensure markers are placed by an experienced paediatric health professional and double-checked by gait laboratory staff via recording software.

steps.title: Randomize Testing Order
steps.instruction: Randomize the order of barefoot and footwear conditions for each toddler.

substeps.instruction: Alternate between barefoot and footwear conditions depending on the day and session.
Record the alternating process in an Excel spreadsheet.

steps.title: Collect Gait Data
steps.instruction: Capture kinematic and spatiotemporal data using the Vicon MX system and GAITRite Electronic Walkway.

substeps.instruction: Perform a static trial: encourage the toddler to stand still with all markers exposed to motion cameras for calibration.

Encourage walking using a parent positioned approximately 1 meter from the end of the GAITRite mat with a favorite toy or food reward, or a post box approximately 1 meter from the end of the mat with a small token/toy to post.
Collect at least three mat passes per testing session to ensure adequate steps.
Allow uncontrolled speed during collection (matching will be performed post-hoc).

steps.title: Process Data
steps.instruction: Clean and extract marker trajectories to create a kinematic model in OpenSim.

substeps.instruction: Visualize all footprints in the software and remove any partial footprints prior to extraction.
Clean, label, and extract measured marker trajectories from Vicon Nexus software and import them into OpenSim.
Scale the segment lengths of the generic 'Gait2392-Simbody' model to each toddler using the static trial markers.
Use inverse kinematics analysis to minimize the difference between measured markers and scaled models to obtain kinematics.
Match within-participant walking speed between trials by excluding data from slow walking or running trials.

steps.title: Analyze Results
steps.instruction: Perform statistical analysis on the extracted gait variables.

substeps.instruction: Collect data from both limbs; if no differences are found between limbs, report data from the right limb only.
Describe gait variables using frequencies (%), means, and standard deviations.
Report maximum and minimum joint angles for the right hip, knee, ankle, and subtalar joint during the stance phase for each condition.
Analyze differences between conditions using linear regression clustered by individual participant with robust variance estimates.
Calculate mean difference, 95% confidence intervals, p-values (significance at p<0.05), and effect sizes (mean difference divided by pooled standard deviation).
